title: "AI-use and verification log"
last-reviewed: "2026-09-08"

Complete a record for a material AI-assisted task while you can still explain the input, the result and your checks. Start the permission and input fields before using the tool; complete verification afterwards.

Store protected prompts and outputs only in an approved environment. Never record credentials. Tailor disclosure to current local and publication requirements.

## Completed example

*Illustrative example; replace these details with your own verified record.*

**Record ID:** AI-012, 28 August 2026
**Task:** propose a minimal test for a de-identified analysis function after the error was reproduced with synthetic data.
**Tool/environment:** institutionally managed coding assistant; version shown in session record.
**Authority:** institutional software guidance checked 27 August; no research data permitted in this workflow.
**Input:** synthetic variable names and invented values; confidential project name, file paths and comments removed.
**Alternative:** manual debugging attempted and failing function isolated first.
**Output used:** one proposed boundary-case test; generated implementation was not accepted unchanged.
**Verification:** researcher explained the expected result, wrote independent known-value tests, ran missing/zero/extreme cases and reviewed the diff. All tests and the session-derived change are linked to commit `abc123` in the controlled repository.
**Limitation:** test coverage does not establish validity of the scientific model.
**Decision-maker:** named analyst.
**Disclosure:** retained in internal methods log; manuscript disclosure will follow the selected journal's current policy.

## Check your record

A useful record lets another authorised person distinguish generated output from the part you checked and accepted. Leave the verification result unresolved until the check actually occurs.

## Scenario test

A generated literature summary is fluent and contains six citations. Verification finds that two DOI records do not exist and another article does not support the sentence. Record the failed output and verification result; do not silently keep the plausible citations. Rebuild the claim from sources you opened and checked, and reconsider whether the tool is suitable for this task.
